• E-bikes like the one shown here can safely
and affordably provide significant
transportation access benefits for many
people.
• However, mis-labeled and misunderstood
devices capable of much higher speeds (AKA
e-motos) are associated with a trend of fatal
crashes across the country, particularly
involving young people.
• While SEMCOG and its partners advocate for
clearer and more effective State laws to
improve safety, communities and families
need to understand e-bikes, e-motos, how
they are different, and how to stay safe.

Observe safe speeds
in all environments

In shared spaces, observe
speed of people walking and/or
riding analog bicycles

• Buyer beware – devices marketed as “e-bikes” often do
not fit the legal requirements of e-bikes (classes 1-3) and
carry significant safety risks
• Wear the right helmet; high-speed e-motos require
motorcycle-grade helmets
